title: Parabolic Long
teaches: The parabolic long as we trade it: Bracco's parabolic burst mirrored, a 3 to 5 day accelerating panic drop that ends on a gap-down climax day, bought only after the turn on the first 5-minute close back over VWAP, the stop a few cents under the climax low, the daily 9 EMA as the target, the one long our 200-day rule allows below the line, and below it only on an index or a levered index ETF, never a single stock (D-009), and a loss taken at the stop as the cost of being a day early.

facts.quote: any time a successful parabolic short goes down 50-60%+ in a few days, that’s the premise for the long setup.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the long comes after a successful parabolic short falls 50-60% or more in a few days.

facts.quote: Entry is opening range highs or the first green 5-minute candle or any range break to the upside if the stock doesn’t rally out of the gate, which they usually do.
facts.claim: Kullamagi's entry: the opening-range high, the first green 5-minute candle or a range break up.

facts.quote: This is by far the riskiest setup if done wrong or if you have issues with not obeying your stops.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: by far the riskiest setup if done wrong or if stops are not obeyed.

facts.quote: Think of stocks as rubber bands, if they get really stretched short term, they can have powerful snapbacks.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: stocks stretched short term snap back like rubber bands.

facts.quote: These things can bounce 50-100% in a few days.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the bounce can be 50% to 100% in a few days.

facts.quote: Don’t be too early. WAIT for the right setup. Let the amateur shorts get run over, that’s where your edge comes in.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: do not be too early; wait for the right setup.

facts.quote: Most of these are short setups, but sometimes there are also good long setups but they don’t occur as often.
facts.claim: Kullamagi: the long version is rarer than the short.

facts.quote: Often price will close well off the low in a SC, reflecting the buying by these large interests.
facts.claim: Wyckoff school: a selling climax often closes well off its low, as large interests buy.

facts.quote: A wave of buying easily pushes prices up; this is further fueled by short covering.
facts.claim: Wyckoff school: the automatic rally is pushed by buying and short covering.

facts.quote: If the ST goes lower than that of the SC, one can anticipate either new lows or prolonged consolidation.
facts.claim: Wyckoff school: a test under the climax low means new lows or a long consolidation.

facts.quote: A Reversal Extension is formed when the price pulls away from the moving averages, then snaps back up and is accompanied by heavy volume.
facts.claim: Kell: a Reversal Extension is a snap back from far under the averages on heavy volume.

facts.quote: Stops are placed just below the low of the Reversal Extension bar. Be quick to take profits and raise stops with the first profit target at the retest of the 20 EMA.
facts.claim: Kell: the stop just below the reversal bar's low; be quick to take profits.

facts.quote: Often, trading the daily Reversal Extension is best avoided.
facts.claim: Kell: trading the daily Reversal Extension is often best avoided.

facts.quote: Get aggressive trading individual stocks when you see a Reversal Extension on the index.
facts.claim: Kell: get aggressive in stocks when the index itself prints a Reversal Extension.

facts.quote: That's when price plunges in a straight line drop, day after day, with little or no overlap between price bars.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: a vertical run down plunges day after day with little overlap between bars.

facts.quote: There is minimal overlap from price bar to bar.
facts.claim: Bulkowski: minimal overlap from bar to bar.

facts.quote: Only try this if the event day decline is a large one, say over 30%.
facts.claim: Bulkowski trades a dead-cat bounce only after a one-day drop over 30%.

facts.quote: Price usually gaps downward, closing 15% to 70% lower than the prior day.
facts.claim: Bulkowski's dead-cat bounce starts with a one-day gap down of 15% to 70%.

facts.quote: This is a deadly sin in the market and one of the worst habits an investor can have. Why try to catch a falling dagger?
facts.claim: O'Neil: buying a falling stock is a deadly sin; why catch a falling dagger.

facts.quote: Stocks that decline more than normal are under heavy liquidation by institutional investors and are almost always down for a reason
facts.claim: O'Neil: stocks that fall more than normal are under heavy liquidation for a reason.

facts.quote: I never go against the long-term trend.
facts.claim: Minervini never goes against the long-term trend.

facts.quote: If a stock’s price is in a long-term downtrend, don’t even consider buying it.
facts.claim: Minervini: do not consider buying a stock in a long-term downtrend.

facts.claim: Bracco: the parabolic burst is a 3-5 day final leg.

facts.quote: Three straight days of gains. The more consecutive up days, the better the setup.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 1: three straight up days (mirrored: three straight down days).

facts.quote: Two consecutive overnight gap ups. This can include the exhaustion gap on the climax day. Unfilled gaps left behind is a bonus.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 2: two consecutive gap ups, the climax gap may count (mirrored: gap downs).

facts.quote: Two out of three days of range expansion, where the percentage gain is larger than the previous day.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 3: two of three days with a bigger percent move than the day before.

facts.quote: Two days of volume expansion, with each day’s volume higher than the last.
facts.claim: Bracco's box 4: two days of rising volume.

facts.quote: You never know exactly when the climax day will hit, but I won’t short without that gap-up.
facts.claim: Bracco will not short without the climax-day gap (mirrored: the gap down).

facts.quote: The climax gap up typically takes place on day 3 to 5 of the move.
facts.claim: Bracco: the climax gap usually comes on day 3 to 5.

facts.quote: While not every criteria needs to be fully satisfied, the more boxes checked, the stronger the setup.

facts.claim: Bracco: the climax day almost always has the heaviest opening volume of the run.

facts.quote: While this setup is more common in small caps, I prefer mid-to-large cap stocks.
facts.claim: Bracco prefers mid to large caps for the setup.

facts.quote: Being too early to a Parabolic Short is a recipe for disaster.
facts.claim: Bracco: being too early is a recipe for disaster.

facts.quote: You’re lucky to get a couple 5-star candidates a year.
facts.claim: Bracco: a couple of 5-star candidates a year.

facts.claim: Bracco's Monday Effect: notable capitulations and turns have come on a Monday.

facts.claim: Bracco's ideal: a gap down or more weakness before the turn.

facts.quote: A stock, index or leveraged ETF that has fallen straight down for 3 to 5 days in an accelerating, panicky burst: the unwind of a blow-off, or a capitulation in a decline.
facts.claim: The context: a straight-down, accelerating 3 to 5 day burst, a blow-off unwind or a capitulation in a decline.

facts.claim: Boxes one to three: three lower closes, two gap-down opens, two of three days losing more than the day before.

facts.quote: (4) two days of rising volume; (5) a gap down on the climax day. Two down days can stand in for three if range and ATR expand sharply.
facts.claim: Boxes four and five: two days of rising volume and a gap down on the climax day.

facts.quote: The burst is 3 to 5 sessions; the climax usually comes on day 3 to 5.
facts.claim: The burst is 3 to 5 sessions; the climax on day 3 to 5.

questions.q: A new trader in the room asks you what a parabolic long is. What's the short answer?
choices: The turn after a 3 to 5 day crash
Riding a stock up its vertical run
A breakout from a quiet base
A bottom that builds over months
questions.answer: The turn after a 3 to 5 day crash
questions.why: It's the turn after a 3 to 5 day crash. Take Bracco's parabolic burst and flip it upside down. A stock falls straight down for days, gaps down one last time, then snaps back. We buy the snap back, never the fall. Think of a rubber band: stretch it that far that fast and it wants to pull back toward its averages. That pull is the edge. It's also why we wait for the turn instead of guessing the bottom.
questions.lesson_line: We buy the snap back, not the fall.

wrong.A breakout from a quiet base: A base is a quiet rest near the highs. This setup has no rest, just a panic fall and a turn.
wrong.Riding a stock up its vertical run: That's the opposite trade, buying the run up. Ours buys the turn after a crash down.
wrong.A bottom that builds over months: That's a slow bottom. We want a straight-down fall of 3 to 5 days, fast and panicky.

questions.simple: It's the snap back after a fast 3 to 5 day crash. We buy the turn, never the fall.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26: the long is the mirror of Bracco's burst down)
fixed before: touched by the old Model Book card question (D-014)

questions.q: Our parabolic long is Bracco's parabolic burst flipped upside down: down days, gap downs and rising volume.
questions.why: True. Bracco wrote up the short side, and his post has no long. His burst is three straight up days and two gap ups. Two of the three days gain more than the day before, volume rises, and the climax day gaps up. Flip that picture and you have our long. Three straight lower closes and two gap downs. Bigger losses on two of the three days, volume climbing, and a gap down to finish it. Same panic, other direction. I like it this way because you learn one picture and read it both ways.
questions.lesson_line: Read Bracco's burst upside down. That's our parabolic long.
questions.simple: True. It's the same five boxes as Bracco's short burst, just pointing down.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26, confirmed 'yes')

questions.q: Where's the target on this one?
choices: The daily 9 EMA, from below
The 50-day, from below
Back to the high before the fall
A set percent bounce off the low
questions.why: The daily 9 EMA, from below. After a crash like this, price is stretched way under its short averages. The 9 EMA is the line the snap back reaches for. Bracco uses it as his target on the parabolic short, and we use the same line for the long. When price gets there, the trade's done. Here it got there inside a week. One thing to know: this was a stock under its 200-day. Today we'd only run this on an index or a levered ETF.
questions.lesson_line: The 9 EMA is the finish line. When price gets there, the trade's done.

wrong.A set percent bounce off the low: A fixed percent ignores the chart. The 9 EMA moves with the stock, so the target follows the price.
wrong.The 50-day, from below: That's asking a lot of a bounce. After a crash the 50-day sits way above. We take the snap back to the 9 EMA.
wrong.Back to the high before the fall: That's hoping for a full V. We take the snap back to the 9 EMA and we're done.

questions.simple: The 9 EMA from below. That's the line the snap back reaches for, and the trade's done there.

deeper.counter: Bracco calls the 9 EMA a magnet for mean reversion on his short. For longs it's less reliable: in our test only about 4 in 10 reached it before the day's low broke. It's the target, not a promise.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (D47) and on the card's own test of longs (c19)
the exit is part of the held trim question (D-013)

questions.q: A crash has dragged everything under the 200-day. On a parabolic long, what are you allowed to buy down there?
choices: An index fund or a levered ETF
A leader that fell with the market
Any stock that's down 30% or more
A stock pulling back to its 50-day
questions.answer: An index fund or a levered ETF
questions.why: An index fund or a levered ETF. Under the 200-day is a hard no for stocks, even on a perfect parabolic setup. A stock under its 200-day is in a downtrend, and one bad story can keep it falling for months. Nothing on its chart tells you the selling is done. An index washes out when the whole crowd panics at once, and that's the snap back we want. So on a crash, that's where the trade goes: the index fund, or a levered fund built on it.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day, stocks are a no. On a crash, trade the index.

wrong.A leader that fell with the market: Still a stock. Under the 200-day a stock is a no, leader or not.
wrong.Any stock that's down 30% or more: How far it fell doesn't change the rule. A stock under its 200-day is a no.
wrong.A stock pulling back to its 50-day: Under the 200-day the 50-day doesn't save it. Stocks down there are a no.

questions.simple: Only an index fund or a levered ETF. A stock under its 200-day is a no, even on this setup.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B26)
its narrowing is a held decision (D-009)

questions.why: The climax day. The buy day is the climax day, the gap-down day. Even then you buy only after the turn, on the first 5-minute close back over VWAP.
questions.lesson_line: The buy day is the climax day. Not the day before, and not a week later.
questions.simple: The buy day is the climax day, the gap-down day. You still wait for the turn before you buy.

reasons: stable definition from the criteria card; no number that changes

questions.q: Before you take a parabolic long, the stock needs an RS rating of 80 or better.
questions.why: False. RS 80 is how we pick leaders for breakouts and pullbacks. A parabolic long is a different animal. The stock just got crushed, so its RS is going to look terrible. That's the whole point of the trade. We're buying a panic, not a leader, so the leader rule doesn't apply here. Same goes for mean-reversion trades.
questions.lesson_line: Leaders need RS. A panic doesn't.
questions.simple: False. RS 80 is for leaders, and here we're buying a panic, so RS doesn't apply.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (C31)

questions.q: The turn just triggered on your parabolic long. How do you get in?
choices: One market order, the full size
Half now, add over the day's high
A limit order well under the price
A starter, then add at the 9 EMA
questions.answer: One market order, the full size
questions.why: One market order, the full size. When the trigger prints, you hit it at market and you're in at one price with one stop. No scaling in. Bracco takes a second entry on his short, but we don't mirror that on the long. These turns move fast. A limit sitting under the price can leave you watching it go without you. Adding later just raises your average on the same stop. Work out your size from the stop before the open, then it's one click.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, one trade.

wrong.Half now, add over the day's high: That's Bracco's second entry on the short, flipped. We don't do it. One price, one stop.
wrong.A limit order well under the price: Snap backs don't wait. A limit under the price can leave you on the sidelines.
wrong.A starter, then add at the 9 EMA: The 9 EMA is where the trade ends. You don't add at your target.

questions.simple: One market order, full size, one price. Adding later only raises your average on the same stop.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (A5)
rebalanced choices: the old key was the longest

questions.q: It's the climax day. The stock gapped down and is still sliding after the open. When exactly do you buy?
choices: First 5-minute close back over VWAP
The first print after the gap down
The last print of the day
A buy stop over yesterday's high
questions.why: The first 5-minute bar that closes back over VWAP, after the low is in. VWAP is the average price everyone has paid today. A stock that gapped down and kept falling has trapped every buyer under it. When it gets back over that line, the sellers just lost the day. That's the turn. Before that you're guessing at the low, and a falling stock can always fall more. Keep a 5-minute chart up with VWAP on it. When a bar closes back over, buy at market.
questions.lesson_line: The right side of the V. VWAP back, after the low. That's the buy.

wrong.The first print after the gap down: That's buying the knife. Nothing has turned yet, and a gap down can keep sliding.
wrong.The last print of the day: We buy the trigger during the day, never the close. By then your stop is a lot further away.
wrong.A buy stop over yesterday's high: After a crash yesterday's high is way up there. The trigger is the VWAP reclaim.

questions.simple: Buy the first 5-minute close back over VWAP after the low. Before that you're guessing at the bottom.

deeper.trap: The named mistake is buying the knife: the gap or the low before the turn. Bracco warns that shorting at the day's highs is a dangerous trap, and the long is the mirror. A gap down that hasn't reclaimed VWAP is still falling.

reasons: the trigger is the card's default while D-003 is pending
mirrors Bracco's VWAP rule (p10)

questions.q: You bought the VWAP reclaim on the climax day. Your stop goes a few cents under that day's low.
questions.why: True. The climax low is the panic low. If price trades back under it, the selling wasn't done and you're wrong. So the stop sits a few cents under it, not right on it. Those few cents keep a quick tick to the exact low from taking you out. Bracco does the mirror on his short: he's out if the day's high is reclaimed. Set the stop first, then let the size come from the distance.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the climax low.
questions.simple: True. Under the climax low means the selling isn't done, so the stop sits a few cents below it.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (A3, F62)

questions.q: You're scanning for parabolic longs. How long should the fast drop into the climax last?
choices: 3 to 5 sessions
One session
Two to three weeks
A month or more
questions.why: 3 to 5 sessions. That's the last, fastest leg of the fall, the panic part. Bracco calls his burst a 3-5 day move that marks the final leg. The climax gap comes on day 3 to 5. One day is a flush in a leader, a different trade. Weeks of selling is a downtrend. A downtrend doesn't snap back the same way, because nobody's panicking. It's just steady selling, and steady selling can keep going.
questions.lesson_line: Three to five days of panic, then the climax.

wrong.Two to three weeks: That's a decline, not a burst. The burst is the fast end of a fall.
wrong.A month or more: A slow grind lower has no panic in it, so there's nothing to snap back from.
wrong.One session: A one-day flush in a leader is a mean-reversion trade. The burst needs 3 to 5 days of panic.

questions.simple: 3 to 5 sessions, the panic leg. Longer is just a downtrend with nothing to snap back from.

reasons: Bracco's burst length and the card agree; two facts

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The smallest climax-day volume we accept is ___ times its 50-day average.
questions.why: 2 times. Our climax day ends at 2 times its 50-day average volume or more, with volume rising through the burst. Bracco's fourth box is two days of rising volume.
questions.lesson_line: A climax without a crowd is not a climax. Two times average, rising.
questions.simple: A climax needs a crowd, so the day's volume must reach at least 2 times the 50-day average.

reasons: +3 the 2x line rests on one cited fact (c06)
+2 a threshold that is a card proposal and can change

questions.q: The stock closed under its lower Bollinger band yesterday. That close is your buy signal.
questions.why: False. A close under the lower Bollinger band says the stock is stretched. That's a plus, not a trigger. Bracco says band breaches are short-lived and often come before a snap back. But stretched can get more stretched. On one index low we wrote it as 'not bottom calling, but stretched'. The buy still waits for the climax day and the first 5-minute close back over VWAP.
questions.lesson_line: Outside the Bollinger band says stretched. It doesn't say buy.
questions.simple: False. A close under the Bollinger band means stretched, not bottomed, so you still wait for the VWAP reclaim.

reasons: stable; Bracco and the card agree

questions.q: You're flipping through charts that fell hard this month. Which one is a parabolic fall?
choices: Steeper legs, bars barely overlap
A stair-step down, dips get bought
A slow drift under the 50-day
Each leg down gets smaller
questions.why: Steeper legs, with bars that barely overlap. Parabolic means the fall speeds up. Each day drops harder than the last and the bars stack straight down. That's panic, and panic is what snaps back. A stair-step with overlapping bars is orderly selling. Somebody big is getting out a little at a time, and that can go on for weeks. So look at the shape before you look at the percent.
questions.lesson_line: Parabolic means the fall speeds up. A stair-step is a different animal.

wrong.A stair-step down, dips get bought: That's orderly. Overlapping bars mean nobody's panicking yet.
wrong.A slow drift under the 50-day: A grind lower is the worst place for this trade. There's no climax to buy.
wrong.Each leg down gets smaller: That fall is slowing down, the opposite. We want each leg steeper.

questions.simple: The one where each leg gets steeper and the bars barely overlap. That's panic, and panic snaps back.

reasons: one choice replaced to remove a silly option; Bulkowski site blocks plain downloads

deeper.counter: Bulkowski's vertical run down describes the same look: price plunges day after day with little or no overlap between price bars.

questions.q: Heavy volume, closing at the low. Is your parabolic long setting up?
questions.story: A stock that topped recently broke a three-month support level yesterday for the first time. Today is its second straight down day. It closes near the low on heavy volume.
choices: Not yet, it's day two of a breakdown
Yes, heavy volume means capitulation
Yes, if it reclaims VWAP tomorrow
No, it needs to be under its 200-day
questions.answer: Not yet, it's day two of a breakdown
questions.why: Not yet. This is day two of a breakdown. The first days of a fall are where the selling starts, not where it ends. Bracco passed on a long in exactly this spot. It was a second down day, and the first break of a 3-month support level. Breaking a level like that brings in fresh sellers. The panic we buy comes after 3 to 5 days, when they're worn out. Put it on your radar and let the burst build.
questions.lesson_line: Day two of a breakdown is the start of the fall, not the end.

wrong.Yes, if it reclaims VWAP tomorrow: A reclaim only counts after a full burst. Two days isn't one.
wrong.Yes, heavy volume means capitulation: Heavy volume on day two is sellers showing up, not sellers finishing.
wrong.No, it needs to be under its 200-day: That's backwards. The 200-day isn't a requirement. For a stock, being under it means we pass.

questions.simple: Not yet. Day two of a breakdown is the start of the selling, and the panic we buy comes later.

reasons: card line plus Bracco's pass; the pass was on QQQ, an index, so the wording stays general

questions.q: The setup's perfect, but the company reports earnings in two days. You don't buy it.
questions.why: True. No new buys in the 3 days before a report. A report can gap the stock right past your stop overnight, and no stop order can catch a gap. On a parabolic long you're already buying a stock in a panic. Stacking an earnings coin flip on top is a risk you don't need. Check the earnings date before you plan any buy.
questions.lesson_line: Check the calendar before the chart. Three days before a report, no new buys.
questions.simple: True. A report can gap the stock past your stop overnight, so no new buys in the 3 days before.

reasons: rests on the owner's rulebook (B22)
the question says 3 sessions, the rulebook says 3 days

questions.q: You're checking the five boxes on a burst down. Which of these isn't one of them?
choices: Volume at 2x the 50-day average
Three straight lower closes
Two gap downs in a row
Two days of rising volume
questions.why: Volume at 2x the 50-day isn't a box. The five are three straight lower closes and two gap downs in a row. Then two of three days losing more than the day before. Then two days of rising volume, and a gap down on the climax day. Big volume on the climax day is something we like to see. It raises the grade. It isn't one of the five, and we don't make it a must.
questions.lesson_line: Count the five boxes. Heavy climax volume is a plus, not a box.

wrong.Two days of rising volume: Box four. Each day's volume beats the one before.
wrong.Three straight lower closes: That's box one, Bracco's three up days flipped.
wrong.Two gap downs in a row: Box two. The climax day can be the second gap.

questions.simple: The 2x volume isn't one of the five boxes. Heavy climax volume raises the grade, nothing more.

questions.q: Your stop just traded. What do you do?
